name: texel-mcp

tools.name: texel_render
tools.description: Compile a skin spec and review it. Returns a review sheet image (front | back | right | left views + raw texture), the review (score, issues with JSON paths and fix hints, art checks, craft advice, suggested next steps) and, on request, the texture (64×64 for a player skin), a text render and a close-up of some parts. Deterministic; never modifies files.

spec.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

file.description: Instead of "spec": a .json spec file in the workspace, e.g. "skins/knight.json". Saves resending the whole spec on every call; texel_patch then edits the file in place.

include.description: Extra outputs. "sheet" is the review image; "ascii" adds a text render for models without vision.

focus.description: Also return a close-up of these parts or groups alone (e.g. ["head"], ["arms"]) from all six sides, large, on gray: for judging a face, a hood or one garment.

tools.name: texel_patch
tools.description: Apply a patch to a spec (update, replace, add or remove layers by id; change palette, legend or meta) and render the result like texel_render. Layers without an id first get "<op>-<index>" and keep it, so the next patch can use the same ids. Entries that cannot apply are skipped and reported. With "spec", returns the patched spec, the review and the sheet. With "file", writes the patched spec back to that file and returns only the review and the sheet.

spec.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

file.description: Instead of "spec": a .json spec file in the workspace, e.g. "skins/knight.json". Saves resending the whole spec on every call; texel_patch then edits the file in place.

patch.description: A patch ({ patch: [{ do: "update", id, set }, …] }) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, section "Patches".

include.description: Extra outputs. "sheet" is the review image; "ascii" adds a text render for models without vision.

tools.name: texel_validate
tools.description: Check a spec for errors and warnings without rendering images. Cheap; use it after every edit.

spec.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

file.description: Instead of "spec": a .json spec file in the workspace, e.g. "skins/knight.json". Saves resending the whole spec on every call; texel_patch then edits the file in place.

tools.name: texel_save
tools.description: Compile a spec and write <path>.png (the skin), <path>.skin.json (the source) and optionally <path>.sheet.png into the workspace (/pkg). Refuses specs with errors.

spec.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

path.description: Output path without extension, relative to the workspace, e.g. "skins/frost-mage".

tools.name: texel_live
tools.description: Start (or reuse) a live session and return a studio URL for the user. While it runs, every texel_render result appears in their open browser tab immediately, so they can watch the skin evolve and give feedback mid-way. Call it before the first render and share the URL with the user.

open.description: Also open the URL in the default browser of the machine running this server.

port.description: Preferred local port (default 4747; the next free one is used if busy).

tools.name: texel_share
tools.description: Store the spec on https://www.texel.dev.br and return a short link (https://www.texel.dev.br/s/<id>) that opens the exact skin in the studio. Falls back to a long self-contained link when offline.

spec.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

tools.name: texel_pull
tools.description: Load the spec behind a Texel share link (https://www.texel.dev.br/s/<id>, a bare id, or a long studio link with #z= / #spec=) so you can keep developing an existing skin. Returns the spec JSON.

link.description: A share link or short id.

tools.name: texel_render_family
tools.description: Expand a family (base spec + variants and/or a matrix of axes) and review every member. Returns a lineup image (front and back of each member, in order) and a per-member score table.

family.description: A skin family ({ kind: "family", base, variants?, matrix? }) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/families

tools.name: texel_save_family
tools.description: Expand a family and write <directory>/<member-id>.png and .skin.json for every member, plus <directory>/lineup.png, into the workspace (/pkg). Refuses families with errors.

family.description: A skin family ({ kind: "family", base, variants?, matrix? }) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/families

directory.description: Output directory relative to the workspace, e.g. "skins/guild".

tools.name: texel_import_png
tools.description: Convert an existing PNG in the workspace into an editable spec, one layer per painted face, palette keys c01…cNN. A player skin (64×64 or legacy 64×32) by default; pass layout for a mob, armor, cape, item or block texture. Rename palette keys to material names before editing.

path.description: Path to a .png file, relative to the workspace.

layout.description: Texture layout of the PNG, e.g. "zombie", "humanoid" (armor), "item". Default: player skin.

tools.name: texel_palette
tools.description: Read a reference PNG in the workspace (concept art, a photo of a figure, another skin) and return its main colors, most common first, each with a role (shadow, midtone, highlight, neutral, accent), as a ready spec "palette" and "legend". Use it to match a reference instead of guessing hex values; derive the other tones with "~" steps.

path.description: Path to a .png file, relative to the workspace.

tools.name: texel_diff
tools.description: Compare two specs pixel by pixel and report which faces changed. Use it to confirm a patch touched only what you intended. Returns the changed-pixel mask over the texture map (magenta = changed).

before.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

after.description: A Texel skin spec (version 1) as a JSON object or JSON text. Format: texel://docs/spec, schema: texel://schema/skinspec.v1

tools.name: texel_get_example
tools.description: Return a complete, working example spec to learn from or fork. Skins: explorer, knight, robot, astronaut, wizard, cozy, winged-pig, miner-zombie, creeper, mud-pig, bronze-armor, banner-cape, ember-blade. Family: guild.

tools.name: texel_read_docs
tools.description: Read a documentation page as markdown. Pages: protocol (Skin Agent Protocol), spec (Skin spec reference), art-guide (Skin art guide), families (Skin families), api (Agent interfaces), install (Install as a tool). Read "spec" before writing your first spec.

instructions:
Texel compiles Minecraft skin specs (JSON: palette + ordered drawing ops) into PNGs: 64×64 player skins by default, and with "layout" also mobs (zombies, skeletons, creepers, pigs, cows, wolves, cats, iron golems…), armor, capes/elytra, items and blocks (texel://docs/spec, section "Layouts"). Protocol texel/1.
Workflow: read the "spec" docs (texel_read_docs or resource texel://docs/spec), draft a spec, call texel_render, look at the returned review sheet image and the issues, fix the weakest area (texel_patch changes a few layers by id), render again, then texel_save and texel_share. To judge one area up close, pass focus (e.g. ["head"]) to texel_render; to match a reference image, start the palette with texel_palette.
Keep the spec in a workspace file and pass "file" instead of "spec" to texel_render, texel_patch and texel_validate: texel_patch then edits the file in place and replies with only the review, so the spec isn't resent on every iteration.
When a person is waiting on the result, call texel_live first and give them the URL: every texel_render then appears in their open studio tab, so they can watch and steer while you work.
For many related skins (teams, factions, tiers), write a family (kind: "family") and use texel_render_family / texel_save_family.
The score only measures technical hygiene; judge appearance from the sheet image against the brief.
